source: segmentation (Blender render with background replaced by white)
time_convention: t = frame / 25; frame = round(t * 25); frame 0 at t = 0
pixel_convention: x right, y down, origin top-left, full-resolution pixels

camera.motion: static (rock mask bbox identical in every frame: x 328-959, y 25-309; no other background)
camera.perspective_cues: none usable: background is uniform white, no ground plane, horizon or vanishing lines. Camera appears to look obliquely down (top surface of rock visible, human seen slightly from above).
camera.focal_length: unknown; must be estimated from a question's depth_info + known size

objects.name: human
objects.description: single small walking person (adult male figure), white/pale shirt, dark grey trousers, very pale head (head barely distinguishable from white background); the only moving object
objects.reference_point: pelvis estimate = (pelvis_x, pelvis_y); pelvis_y = foot_y - 0.53 * height_px; pelvis_x = mean mask x in rows +-3 px of pelvis_y. Smoothed version in pelvis_*_smooth (Savitzky-Golay, 11 frames, linear)
objects.image_motion: straight line down-right in the image, direction ~52 deg below +x axis; net ~56 px over 74 frames (~0.77 px/frame mean, roughly uniform; ~0.86 px/frame first 10 frames, ~0.61 last 10 per smoothed track - edge effects of smoothing make this uncertain)

apparent_height_px.note: constant within noise -> camera distance roughly constant over clip; raw per-frame values jitter +-3 px from faint head pixels and stride

apparent_width_px.note: side-on-ish body width incl. arms/legs swing, range 17-20

objects.name: rock
objects.description: large pale/white rock or boulder (mountain-like, with brown/dark eroded faces on its right side), upper part of the frame, to the upper right of the human
objects.note: right tip reaches x = 959 (image edge) so horizontal extent may be truncated by a few px; leftmost point x=328 at y~170; top y=25 near x~530; bottom y=309 near x~690. Bottom-centre of rock outline ~ (690, 309).

events.note: already in motion at frame 0, still walking at frame 74; no stops, no direction change
